[[Winter Park, Florida]] }} '''Austin James Rivers''' (born August 1, 1992, in Santa Monica, California) is an American college basketball player for [[Duke University]]. Rivers led [[Winter Park High School]] to back-to-back Florida 6A state championships in 2010 and 2011. He also played in the 2011 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] for the USA National Team, and in addition, Rivers also participated in the 2011 McDonald's All-American Game. Rivers was one of the top rated high school basketball players in the class of 2011, being rated as high as No. 1 by Rivals.com. On September 30, 2010, Rivers committed to [[Duke University]]. His father, [[Doc Rivers]], coaches the [[Boston Celtics]]. His older brother, [[Jeremiah Rivers]], plays for [[KK Mega Vizura]] in Serbia. His older sister, Callie Rivers, played volleyball for the University of Florida. ==High School== Rivers was ranked #1 by [[Rivals.com]],{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2288 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for the class of 2011 |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date= |accessdate=August 24, 2010| archiveurl= http://web.archive.org/web/20100819085607/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2288| archivedate= 19 August 2010 | deadurl= no}} while being rated as the #3 player by [[ESPN]]{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2011&action=upsell&=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com% appRedirect 2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2011 |title=College Basketball Recruiting - ESPNU 100 - 2011 |publisher=ESPN.com |date= |accessdate=August 24, 2010}} and [[Scout.com]].{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2011 |title=Scout.com: Men's Basketball Recruiting |publisher=Scout.com |date= |accessdate=August 24, 2010}} In 2010, Rivers led [[Winter Park High School]] to the school's first state title in a 76-57 win against [[Dr. Phillips High School]] in the 6A state championship. Rivers scored 23 points in the game.{{cite web|url=http://www.theledger.com/article/20100306/news/3065036?p=1&tc=pg |title=Rivers Leads Winter Park to Title |publisher=TheLedger.com |date=March 6, 2010 |accessdate=August 28, 2010}} In June 2010, Rivers was a part of the gold medal winning team at the FIBA Americas U18 Championship. He set a team USA record for an U18 event with 35 points against [[Canada]].{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/luke_winn/07/02/rivers.notes/index.html |title=Austin Rivers impressed many with his performance at FIBA tourney |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date=July 2, 2010 |accessdate=August 24, 2010| archiveurl= http://web.archive.org/web/20100824113114/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/luke_winn/07/02/rivers.notes/index.html| archivedate= 24 August 2010 | deadurl= no}} On August 5, 2010, Rivers was named to the 5th annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 game,{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/high-school-wire/2010/08/elite-24-roster-revealed-first-12/ |title=Elite 24 Roster Revealed (First 12) |publisher=Slam Online |date=August 5, 2010 |accessdate=August 28, 2010| archiveurl= http://web.archive.org/web/20100806080459/http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/high-school-wire/2010/08/elite-24-roster-revealed-first-12/| archivedate= 6 August 2010 | deadurl= no}} where he was named co-MVP. He had 25 points, 4 rebounds, and 4 assists.{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball/os-hs-austin-rivers-elite-24-20100828,0,7416783.story |title=Austin Rivers is named co-MVP at ESPN all-star event |publisher=OrlandoSentinel.com |date=August 28, 2010 |accessdate=}} On March 5, 2011, Rivers led Winter Park to back to back Florida 6A state championships with a 52-44 victory over [[Dr. Phillips High School]], in which he had 25 points, 11 rebounds, and 4 steals.{{cite web|author=Collings, Buddy |url=http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2011-03-05/sports/os-hs-6a-state-boys-final-20110305_1_billydee-williams-shane-larkin-brett-comer |title=Winter Park repeats as 6A champ with win over Dr. Phillips |publisher=Orlando Sentinel |date=March 5, 2011 |accessdate=March 22, 2011}} Rivers was named the 2011 [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] on March 10, 2011.{{cite web|author=Payne, Greg Go UNC!!!|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4681563/austin-rivers-earns-national-honor |title=Austin Rivers earns national honor |publisher=ESPNBoston.com |date=March 11, 2011 |accessdate=March 22, 2011}} He was also an All-American and All-State Guard. In addition, he played at the 2011 Nike Hoop Summit and on the [[USA]] national team. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2011}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Austin Rivers | position = SG | hometown = Winter Park, FL | highschool =Winter Park High School | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 190 |40 = | commitdate = September 30, 2010 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} |} http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=3586209 ==College career== Rivers committed to [[Duke University]] on September 30, 2010, over Kansas and UNC.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=5632647 |title=Austin Rivers commits to Duke over Kansas and UNC. |publisher=ESPN.com |date=September 30, 2010 |accessdate=}} His commitment was widely covered by ESPN and various other sports networks given his status as the Class of 2011's top recruit. As a freshman, Rivers played in Duke's exhibition games in China and Dubai during an international tour in August, 2011. In the first game against the [[China men's national basketball team]], Rivers scored 18 points on 8-15 shooting and led Duke to an 77-64 victory. In the second game (also against the Chinese National Team), Rivers scored 12 points in a 78-66 victory, making several rim-shattering dunks during the first half. In the final game played in Beijing, China, Rivers chipped in 11 points as Duke topped the Chinese, 93-78. [http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=205245948]. In his team's 86-66 victory over the Dubai National Team, he scored 16 points, including 10 in the second quarter, on an array of impressive drives. At Duke's annual Midnight Madness event, Countdown to Craziness, Rivers had 14 points and 5 rebounds in 24 minutes to lead the White team in the inter-squad scrimmage. On February 8, 2012, his 3-point basket as time expired allowed Duke to overcome an 82-72 deficit with 2 minutes to play in an 85-84 victory over the [[University of North Carolina]]. The victory ended North Carolina's 31 game winning streak at the [[Dean Smith Center]].{{cite news |url=http://www.basketinside.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=9129:basketinsidecom-talking-with-austin-rivers-of-duke-university&catid=36:rubriche&Itemid=59 |title=Talking with Austin Rivers of Duke University |publisher=Basketinside.com |date=March 1, 2012}} ==NBA career== On March 26, 2012. Duke announced that Rivers was leaving the school to enter the NBA draft. Rivers wrote on Twitter: "I just want to thank all the fans that have supported me this year. it was so fun playing there and becoming a part of the Duke family! … I appreciate everybody, and the support y’all have given me! Duke nation has truly made me a better person and player! Duke #1" Rivers said that he would love to play for his father's team, the Celtics, if they were to select him. {{cite web|last=Bean|first=DJ|title=AUSTIN RIVERS: 'I WOULD LOVE TO' PLAY FOR C'S|url=http://www.weei.com/sports/boston/this-just-in/21188126/austin-rivers-i-would-love-play-cs|publisher=WEEI Radio}} ==Personal life== Rivers is the son of [[Boston Celtics]] head coach [[Doc Rivers]].{{cite news|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/campusrivalry/post/2010/07/dad-says-austin-rivers-to-slow-it-down-and-wait-on-recruiting-trail/1 |title=Dad says Austin Rivers 'to slow it down and wait' on recruiting trail |publisher=USA Today |date=July 28, 2010 |accessdate=August 24, 2010}}{{Cite news |url=http://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F00610F838580C7B8EDDA80894DB494D81 |title=Moving Is Just Part of the Game Plan |first=Lena |last=Williams |date=January 28, 1993 |newspaper=[[New York Times]] }} His older brother, [[Jeremiah Rivers|Jeremiah]] played basketball for [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] before transferring to play for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], while his older sister Callie played volleyball for the [[University of Florida]] and currently plays professionally in Puerto Rico. His favorite team is the Boston Celtics. ==Awards/Honors== *2010 Fiba America U18 Champion *2010 Fiba America U18 MVP *2010 Boost Mobile Elite team selection *2010 Boost Mobile Elite co-MVP *2011 Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award [[James A.
